## Natural history notes

A small, nonnative land snail characterized by its pale whitish to light tan, narrow, pointed shell. In Florida, it is increasingly found in disturbed habitats such as agricultural fields, citrus groves, gardens, landscaped areas, and urban or suburban sites. It is most active in moist conditions and feeds on decaying plant material and sometimes living plant tissue, often clustering on vegetation, irrigation equipment, and other surfaces.
